catalog_quote: [p. 71] In a large central area covering most of Gipuzkoa and parts of Bizkaia and Navarre, the general rule is postinitial accent (on the second syllable), with some exceptional words receiving, instead, initial accent. The general pattern is illustrated by examples such as gizóna 'the man', gizónari 'to the man', gizónarena 'the one of the man', txistúlaria 'the flutist', txistúlariari 'to the flutist'. In most varieties with postinitial accent, final prominence is avoided, with accent retraction to the initial syllable in bisyllabic forms: néska 'the girl', neskári 'to the girl'. ... In Standard Basque, postinitial accent is the dominant pattern among speakers of this variety. [p. 102] Stress is generally post-initial, i.e., on the second syllable of the word, although some exceptional words show initial stress. sweep_summary: Basque (basq1248, catalog kind 'lexical', deciding source Hualde 2003 sec. 2.2.4 Zuberoan). 24 title hits: 9 are other languages or general theory (Clemens, Eychenne, Leben, Melvold, Enguehard, Wagner, Nouveau, Boukous, Hammond). The 15 Basque items are almost all Hualde's De Gruyter/Benjamins/Elsevier papers (1993 Getxo, 1993 Diachronica, 1996 reconstruction, 1998 Azkoitia, 1999 'Basque accentuation', 2000 Markina, 2002 dialectology, 2002 LabPhon pitch-to-stress [Glottolog lists it twice], 2003 western shift, 2007 convergence) — all paywalled (De Gruyter serves only a bot challenge; ScienceDirect 403); only the Diachronica abstract was reachable ('in a large central area there is no contrastive word accent, systems with phonologically distinctive accentuation are found both in eastern and western regions'). fetched sources and read: Elordieta & Selkirk 2018 (open, UCSC festschrift) — Lekeitio Northern Bizkaian has a lexical accented/unaccented contrast with the HL accent fixed on the penultimate of accented words; confirms the lexical coding for a western variety. Ito 2002 (UIUC) is on IDEALS but its PDF is access-restricted (abstract only; focus intonation in Bermeo Basque, not placement). Aurrekoetxea et al. 2012 'Stress areas' (LimiAr proceedings) and the undated Hualde Souletin manuscript could not be located. Best first-hand statement read: the held Hualde 1997 monograph sec. 4.2-4.3 (Zuberoan penultimate by rule with lexically marked oxytones), which confirms and does not supersede the catalog's Hualde 2003 passage. Highest-priority unread item remains Hualde 1999 'Basque accentuation' (van der Hulst vol.). DuckDuckGo/OpenAlex/Semantic Scholar rate-limited or refused; Bing returned junk), so 'not-found' items had only Crossref, Glottolog, IDEALS and publisher pages behind them. .

new_statements.translation: In a wide eastern region the accent generally goes on the penultimate syllable; that is, the main rule is [-2]. This accentuation extends from Zuberoa and Erronkari to Baztan and Ultzama. [...] In some of these varieties, such as Zuberoan and above all Roncalese, lexical and morphological exceptions create accentual contrasts. [...] In Zuberoan the accent is normally placed on the penultimate syllable. [...] Not all words show this pattern, however. Sometimes the accent goes on the final syllable. To begin with, we have genuine lexical exceptions

Ch. 4 'Ekialdeko azentubidea', sec. 4.2 (p. 74) and sec. 4.3.1 'Zuberoa: azentu patroiak flexiogabeko oinarrietan' (pp. 75-76).
new_statements.reading: Hualde's own fullest treatment: the eastern type (Zuberoan included) is penultimate by rule, with a class of lexically marked oxytones (arrés, andé, etc.), plus predictable finals in glide-final and nasal-vowel-final words and after lexically accented monosyllabic suffixes (-ñi, -tiar, -kor). Read from the held scanned; '[-2] da' normalises the scanned garble '~2] cia'. This is the same description the catalog's deciding 2003 passage condenses and it confirms the 'lexical' coding for Zuberoan (penultimate default + marked oxytonic pattern). Among items actually read this sweep, Elordieta & Selkirk 2018 adds the Lekeitio (Northern Bizkaian) lexical accented/unaccented contrast with fixed penultimate placement in accented words.

sources.citation: Elordieta, Gorka & Elisabeth Selkirk (2018). Notes on prosodic headedness and tone in Tokyo Japanese, Standard English and Northern Bizkaian Basque. In Hana-bana: A Festschrift for Junko Ito and Armin Mester (UCSC, online). [Glottolog 612507]
sources.quote: in NBB, there is a lexical contrast between accented and unaccented words, like in Tokyo Japanese. [...] In the particular variety of NBB on which we will base our analysis (the one of Lekeitio), main prosodic prominence is always found on a fixed syllable in an accented word, regardless of the location of that syllable with respect to the accented morpheme. This syllable is the penultimate of the whole word, which may consist of a bare root with no overt affix or a root plus one or more affixes. A falling accent HL surfaces on this penult syllable.
sources.locator: sec. 4 'Northern Bizkaian Basque', paragraphs before ex. (24) (txt lines 674-696)
sources.note: First-hand (Elordieta is the Lekeitio specialist): Northern Bizkaian Basque has a lexical accented/unaccented contrast; accented words carry a HL pitch accent on the penultimate syllable of the whole word (libúru 'book', liburuári, lagunári vs unaccented lagun, lagunena); unaccented words have no word-level prominence and cannot form a phonological phrase alone. Confirms the catalog's 'lexical' kind for a different (western) variety from the Zuberoan deciding passage; theoretical paper, not a survey.

sources.citation: Gandarias, Leire, Iñaki Gaminde, Lorea Unamuno & Aitor Iglesias. 2015. 'Euskara estandarraren korrelatu akustikoez' [On the acoustic correlates of Standard Basque]. Euskalingua 26: 6-13. (open, mendebalde.eus)
sources.quote: Instrumental (duration, F0, intensity) study of one Standard-Basque speaker (Basauri) reading a word list: 'Azentua duten bokalak hitzen lehenengo edo bigarren silabetan bakarrik aurki ditzakegu' [accented vowels are found only in the first or second syllable of words]; table 10: 446 accented vowels in syllable 2 vs 72 in syllable 1. Duration and energy separate accented from unaccented vowels; F0 falls sharply after the accent.

sources.quote: Ataun speaker: in both home dialect and Standard Basque the unmarked pattern is [+2] ('patroi ez markatua [+2] dela, hau da, azentuaren norabidea ezkerretik hasita bigarren silabak darama'); in Standard Basque the speaker drops the dialect's plural pre-accenting and nearly all lexically marked (initial-accent) words (only básoa 'glass' vs basóa 'forest' survives); cites Gaminde 2005:270 that in Standard Basque [+2] 'arau bilakatzen da eta salbuespenik gabe bete' [becomes the rule and applies without exception].
